8.title: Plating on ABS and ABS/PC: Principles and Plating Systems
8.excerpt: Plastic does not conduct electricity, so the surface must be made conductive before plating. This article explains the main steps and the four plating systems HANIN runs on ABS.
8.body:
## 1. Why Plastic Needs Its Own Process
ABS and ABS/PC plastic do not conduct electricity and have a smooth surface, so metal does not bond to them directly. Plastic plating therefore has two parts: surface treatment to create a conductive, adhesive base, then electroplating the metal layers.

## 2. Main Steps
- Degrease and clean the part surface.
- Etch to create micro-roughness so the metal layer bonds.
- Neutralize, then activate with HCl and palladium to form a conductive seed layer.
- Plate the metal layers, finishing with a nickel-chrome layer.
- Inspect appearance and plating thickness, and test durability per customer requirements.

## 3. Plating Systems HANIN Runs on ABS and ABS/PC
| Plating system | Surface character | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nickel Chrome 3+ | Bright, glossy | Trivalent chrome system |
| Nickel Chrome 6+ | Bright, glossy | Hexavalent chrome system |
| Satin Nickel | Fine matte, low reflection | For parts that need a matte surface |
| Black Nickel Chrome | Deep black | For dark decorative parts |

A hairline finish can also be made on the nickel chrome layer on request.

## 4. Notes When Designing Parts
- The plastic surface and mold quality directly affect appearance after plating.
- Sharp corners, deep holes and recesses are hard to plate evenly, so discuss with the engineers before finalizing the drawing.
- How the part is hung on the rack must be planned from the start to avoid contact marks on visible faces.

## 5. Applications
Lamp bezels, vehicle grille trim, control knobs, logos and raised lettering on cars, motorcycles and home appliances.

Send a drawing or sample through the Contact page so HANIN engineers can assess platability.

9.title: Surface Pretreatment Before Plating: Why It Decides Adhesion
9.excerpt: Most plating peeling and pitting starts from a surface that is not clean or not properly activated. This article describes the pretreatment sequence at the HANIN factory.
9.body:
## 1. The Role of Pretreatment
Plating adheres well only when the metal or plastic substrate is free of oil and oxide and has a uniform surface state. Any deviation here shows up after plating as peeling, pitting, discoloration or uneven plating.

## 2. The Pretreatment Sequence at HANIN
- Goods receipt and storage: sorted by substrate material and plating requirement.
- Ultrasonic degreasing: removes oil, grease and machining residue trapped in narrow gaps and small holes.
- HCl tank: removes oxide and rust on metal substrates.
- Surface activation: brings the surface to a state ready to accept the plating.
- Water rinse between steps: avoids carrying chemicals into the next tank.

## 3. Common Defects Linked to Pretreatment
| Symptom | Common pretreatment cause |
| --- | --- |
| Peeling, flaking plating | Oil or oxide remaining; insufficient activation |
| Pitting, spots | Surface impurities or incomplete rinsing |
| Uneven plating | Non-uniform surface between areas |
| Discoloration after plating | Pretreatment chemicals left in crevices |

## 4. What Customers Can Do to Help
- State the substrate material and the previous processing (cutting oil, stamping oil, mold release).
- Avoid bare-hand contact or rust on parts before plating.
- Pack parts so they are not scratched or contaminated in transit.

Tank parameters (concentration, temperature, time) are set for each part type and are not published in this article.

10.title: Electrolytic vs Electroless Nickel: Differences and How to Choose
10.excerpt: The two nickel plating types give different properties. This article compares them on the criteria engineers commonly use when choosing a plating for metal parts.
10.body:
## 1. Two Ways to Form a Nickel Layer
Electrolytic nickel uses electric current to deposit nickel on the part. Electroless nickel forms the nickel layer by a chemical reaction in solution, with no external current. Different ways of forming the layer lead to different properties.

## 2. Comparison
| Criterion | Electrolytic nickel | Electroless nickel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Appearance | Bright, glossy, decorative | Even surface |
| Hardness, wear resistance | Medium | Higher, good wear resistance |
| Heat resistance | Ordinary | Good |
| Uniformity on complex shapes | Depends on current distribution | More even at corners and holes |
| Typical applications | Handles, bolts, hinges, locating pins | Gears, pins, shafts, machine plates |

The table is a qualitative comparison only. Specific values such as hardness or thickness are agreed for each order.

## 3. How to Choose
- Need a bright, durable look: electrolytic nickel, optionally topped with chrome.
- Need wear resistance, heat resistance or an even layer on complex parts: electroless nickel.
- Parts with threads or narrow slots: say so, so engineers can allow for plating tolerance.

## 4. Lines at HANIN
Electrolytic nickel, electroless nickel, black nickel and black manganese phosphating run on the barrel plating and semi-automatic rack plating lines, depending on part size and quantity.

Send a drawing with hardness, thickness and acceptance standard requirements to get advice on a suitable plating.

11.title: Plating Inspection: Thickness, NSS/CASS Salt Spray, Hull Cell Test
11.excerpt: The measurements and tests HANIN uses to control plating tanks and evaluate finished goods, with the actual equipment at the factory.
11.body:
## 1. Two Groups of Inspection
Plating quality control has two parts: controlling the solution in the tank (before and during plating) and inspecting finished goods (after plating).

## 2. Equipment at the HANIN Factory
| Inspection | Equipment | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Solution analysis | Analysis lab and analytical chemicals | Keep tank composition within the working range |
| Plating tank test | Hull cell tester | Assess plating across different current density zones |
| Plating thickness | APC-100 gauge | Confirm thickness against the requirement |
| Corrosion resistance | Neutral salt spray (NSS) | Assess corrosion resistance |
| Corrosion resistance (acid) | Acid salt spray (CASS) | Faster test for multi-layer decorative plating |

## 3. NSS and CASS Salt Spray
NSS uses a neutral salt fog, while CASS uses an acid salt fog with added copper salt, so corrosion conditions are harsher. Test duration and pass criteria are agreed with the customer for each product.

## 4. Inspection After Spray Painting
For painted and printed parts, the factory has a set of 10 reliability test devices: RCA abrasion, hot water, high temperature and humidity, UV measurement, alcohol/eraser rubbing, pencil rubbing, drop test, thickness measurement, polishing and bending.

## 5. How to Read the Results
- State the measuring location and number of measuring points when requesting a thickness report.
- State the pass criteria when requesting a salt spray test (duration, allowed level of rust).
- Test samples should match the actual part and plating process.

Send acceptance criteria with the drawing so HANIN can confirm the inspection plan.
